title: An LC circuit whose coil holds a shorted inner coil of half the area and half the length: self and mutual inductance, flux exclusion and the resonant frequency
summary: A glowing LC bench: a long solenoid with a shorted inner coil of half its area and half its length. Close the switch and the inner coil's current pushes the magnetic field out of its core - a quarter of the volume - so the effective inductance falls to 3L/4 and the resonance rises to 2/sqrt(3LC), watched on an oscilloscope and a frequency sweep, with every option audited.
subject: Physics
topic: Self and mutual inductance of coaxial solenoids - a shorted coil lowers the effective inductance and raises the LC resonance
subtopics: Self-inductance of a long solenoid, L = mu0 n^2 A l
Mutual inductance of coaxial solenoids, M = mu0 n1 n2 (common area)(common length)
A resistance-free shorted coil keeps its flux linkage fixed: L2 dI2/dt + M dI1/dt = 0
Effective inductance L_eff = L1 - M^2/L2 = L1 (1 - k^2)
concepts: The inner coil has 2N turns per length over d/2 - the same N d turns - on area S/2, so L2 = mu0 (2N)^2 (S/2)(d/2) = L
The outer field mu0 N I1 threads the inner coil's turns over its area: M = mu0 N (2N)(S/2)(d/2) = L/2
With no resistance the shorted coil's EMF is zero, so I2 = -(M/L2) I1 = -I1/2, and the field inside it vanishes
The field is expelled from (S/2)(d/2) = a quarter of the volume, so L_eff = L - M^2/L2 = 3L/4
omega = 1/sqrt(L_eff C) = 2/sqrt(3LC); for coaxial solenoids L_eff = L(1 - a l) whatever the inner turns

methods: Solved independently: L2 = L, M = L/2, zero EMF round the shorted coil, L_eff = L - M^2/L2 = 3L/4, omega = 2/sqrt(3LC) - option C
sympy: inductances from mu0 n^2 A l and mu0 n1 n2 A l; L_eff and omega derived; only option C matches
scipy integration of the coupled circuit (no L_eff used): measured omega sqrt(LC) = 1.154701, I2 = -I1/2 throughout, energy conserved
Field energy: flux conservation fixes I2, Ampere's law gives B = 0 in the core, the energy integral gives L_eff = 3L/4
Controls: open coil omega sqrt(LC) = 1; other turns, areas and lengths always 1/sqrt(1 - a l)
Every option audited by the inductance it implies: A 15L/16, B 5L/36, C 3L/4, D 3L/2 = L + M
